name: What is the difference between a general contractor and a design-build firm for ground-up construction?

mainEntity.name: Should a homeowner hire a general contractor, a design-build company, or separate architect and builder for a new home?
mainEntity.text: Should a homeowner hire a general contractor, a design-build company, or separate architect and builder for a new home?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right delivery method depends on the owner’s goals and how much coordination they want to manage. A general contractor usually enters after plans are developed and focuses on building the approved design. A design-build firm combines design and construction, which can speed up decisions and reduce handoff problems. Separate architect-and-builder arrangements may provide more independent oversight but often require more owner involvement and coordination. For ground-up projects in Los Angeles, the best fit often comes down to budget certainty, schedule, design complexity, and how involved the homeowner wants to be in decision-making. If the project is highly custom, integrated design and construction can help control feasibility and cost from the beginning. If the owner already has a strong design team, a separate builder may be a better fit.
acceptedAnswer.description: A general contractor typically builds from plans prepared by others, while a design-build firm manages both design and construction under one team. Separate architect-and-builder setups can give more independent oversight but require more coordination. For ground-up construction, the best choice depends on how much control, speed, and integration the owner wants.
